notes:
Method: static read only. The review tools allowed no git or cargo runs, so I did not execute tests, clippy or the dry-run publish. The worktree's gitdir HEAD file reads 330986f574914ada17e79d074227527cce4eb9ba (matches the input commit). The branch name was not independently confirmed, because HEAD there is detached.

RULE-ADR-PLAN: the sprint doc's adrs list covers every binding repo-level ADR the sprint touches. There are no per-crate ADRs: docs/sc-jev-check/architecture.md holds no ADR sections. ADR-SAG-0025 and the four r-2b amendments are deliverables, and every listed id resolves to an Active ADR.

RULE-ADR-CODE: judge is called once per backend (run/mod.rs:568). Base validation happens before the first send (run/mod.rs:553). ChainContext requests are re-validated before their own send (run/mod.rs:659) and a refusal becomes a Failed backend with NotSent attestation and no log event. All-failed returns Err and leak is any Failed. A session-save failure keeps the answers and adds one warning with the code only. Digest recovery runs before send_with_busy_retry on the serialized body. It is attestation-only and never feeds the wire body. Its errors carry only a category and position (JevError::encode_failed) or fixed strings. There is no new disallowed_methods or allow(...) in the crates, no new ResolvedApiKey::as_str call, and test-util is non-default.

RULE-ADR-AWAIT-MUTEX: not applicable. The three owned crates (sc-jev, sc-jev-backends, sc-jev-check) contain no .await, and the Mutex uses in changed test files are synchronous.

Observations, not findings: the test-util WireFault public type family is recorded in the sprint doc and boundary notes but has no ADR of its own. It is feature-gated and covered by the ADR-SAG-0022 and ADR-SAG-0023 test-util convention, so I did not raise it. The ADR-SAG-0024 text ('RunConfig has no mode setter until r-2b') is time-qualified and still accurate.
